Look into prepaid - it can be much cheaper.

For example, Cricket Wireless or StraightTalk. Cricket uses AT&T's network, but they are prepaid and usually cheaper. Four lines here cost $100/month flat, whereas with AT&T you'll pay ~$120 - $130 a month but with 300MB of data (more with 2GB). The only downside, for the most part, is they cap their network speeds - 8Mbps for LTE and 4Mbps for HSPA.

Next up is StraightTalk. 5GB of data for $45/month on AT&T's network. I'm not sure if they have a family plan, anymore.

As for phones, you can buy them outright. If you want something cheap but good, a Moto G LTE is a great choice. OnePlus One or Two, refurb Nexus 5, etc. are also good options.

I did a pretty thorough look at this recently- I can't find the exact numbers, but here's the highlights. YMMV

  1. TMO is by far the cheapest, but their coverage sucks. Good enough in metro areas, but good luck trying to get Maps to connect when your away from the cities and need an alternate route around interstate highway traffic. Uses GSM, though, so phones are fairly portable. Great customer service.

  2. Sprint isn't expensive, but their network sucks more than TMOs. And they use CDMA, so phones are harder to port to a new carrier.

  3. AT&T isn't cheap, although less expensive than Verizon. Awesome coverage where I live, including aforementioned "middle of nowhere trying to use Maps". And they use GSM. That's who we're using now. Crap customer service, although their 3rd party retailers are far better.

  4. Verizon. Great network, not worth the price. Crap customer service.

  5. Straight Talk: MVNO that uses AT&T's network. Has a data cap, but it's a bottleneck, rather than an added charge. Low cost plans, but no family plans. Not cost effective for a family, but one or two people could get a good deal. Customer service isn't good, but it's better than some.

  6. Net10: MVNO that uses TMO. No data cap, but has TMO's crap network. Same price as Straight Talk, customer service is even worse.

  7. Republic Wireless: MVNO that uses Sprint, but also uses VOIP when connected to WiFi. No choice in phones, though. They only have one or two. Great rates, but again- no family plans.

  8. Google Fi: Probably the cheapest plans and uses TMO and Sprint networks. Of course, you have to drop something like $650 for a Nexus 6, since that's the only phone that can use Fi.
